claims.claim_text: The code before yield runs before the app starts handling requests (startup), and the code after yield runs after handling requests (shutdown) [1][3].
claims.reason: Both passages explicitly explain that code before the yield in the lifespan context manager runs during startup before the app starts receiving requests, and code after the yield runs at shutdown after handling requests.

claims.claim_text: Alternatively, you can use event handlers declared with @app.on_event("startup") and @app.on_event("shutdown") to run functions before startup and during shutdown [2].
claims.reason: The passage explicitly describes declaring event handler functions with @app.on_event("startup") and @app.on_event("shutdown") to run code before startup and during shutdown, including examples and details matching the claim.

claims.claim_text: The deprecated alternative approach also uses startup/shutdown event handlers, but if you provide a lifespan parameter, those will not be called [2].
claims.reason: Passage [2] explicitly states that if you provide a `lifespan` parameter, `startup` and `shutdown` event handlers will no longer be called and that it's either `lifespan` or events, matching the claim.

claims.claim_text: So, define a lifespan context manager and yield around startup/setup code and teardown/cleanup code, or use @app.on_event("startup") and @app.on_event("shutdown") handlers [3][2].
claims.reason: Passage [3] shows defining a lifespan context manager with yield via the FastAPI lifespan parameter for startup and shutdown logic, and passage [2] documents using @app.on_event("startup") and @app.on_event("shutdown") as an alternative.

claims.claim_text: The code after the yield will be executed after the application has finished handling requests (i.e., during shutdown) [1][3].
claims.reason: Passages [1] and [3] explicitly state that code after the yield in the asynccontextmanager-based lifespan function is executed after the application has finished handling requests (during shutdown).

claims.claim_text: It unloads or cleans up resources, such as releasing models or other resources, when the application stops.
claims.reason: The cited passages show a lifespan context manager that loads models before the yield and explicitly clears/unloads them after the yield, stating this runs on shutdown to release resources.
